ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.subtitle: Every financial event on this asset, with the running cost, accumulated depreciation and net book value after each one, and a link to the journal it posted.
ledger.openingHint: Seed the historical cost and accumulated depreciation of an asset that already exists, so the sub-ledger reconciles from day one. This posts one balanced opening journal.

reconciliation.title: Asset reconciliation
reconciliation.explainer: The proof that the fixed-asset sub-ledger equals the General Ledger control accounts, to the Rappen. A non-zero difference is drift: it blocks the period close until it is explained or corrected.
reconciliation.checkBalanced: Balanced: every control account reconciles for {period}. The period close may proceed.
reconciliation.checkDrift: Drift on {count} control account(s) for {period}. The period close is blocked until it is corrected.

empty.hint: No fixed assets carry a control-account balance at this cut-off.

reports.explainer: Read-only reports across the whole fixed-asset register: the inventory for the auditor's binder, a depreciation forecast for budgeting, the disposal gain/loss pack, what was capitalised, net book value by dimension, and what is reaching end of life.

disposal.title: Dispose asset
disposal.explainer: A disposal is a terminal, posted event: it clears the asset cost and its accumulated depreciation, recognises the proceeds and the book gain or loss, and removes the asset from the active register. A wrong disposal is corrected by reversing the journal, never undone.

depreciationRun.title: Depreciation runs
depreciationRun.subtitle: Calculate the period-end depreciation for every eligible asset, review it, and post it as one balanced journal. A material error is corrected by reversing the run, never by editing history.

depreciationRun.postConfirmBody: This posts the period's depreciation as one balanced journal for {count} asset(s), CHF {total}. It is corrected only by reversing the run, never by editing history.
depreciationRun.reverseHint: The reversal books a mirror entry and gives the depreciation back to every asset in the run. Say why: the reason is recorded on the reversing entry and on the asset movement.

FixedAssets.title: Fixed assets
FixedAssets.body:
Fixed assets: every capitalised asset is created from a category and inherits its depreciation rules and accounts; only what differs is overridden.

Depreciation runs compute and post the periods. Reconciliation compares the register against the ledger's book values.

Once an asset is posted its financial fields lock. Corrections run through postings, not by rewriting the asset.
